situation (example wording): "Robberies in Texas in 2024", "Carjackings in Texas in 2024", "Murders in the US by victim-offender relationship", "Murders in Ohio this year": a state or national question
what the app does today: State and national NIBRS figures are not built; Part I counts route to Historical (P01).
proposed behavior: By what the question asks: one of the seven Part I offenses at state or national level comes from the Crime Index's already-calculated state and national figures (no NIBRS agency summing, no splicing). A NIBRS-only offense or detail goes to NIBRS, summing the agencies that reported, with coverage caveats (agencies and population covered). Any murder detail (weapon, relationship, circumstance, a victim's or offender's sex, race or age) goes to Homicide Reports, one agency or many, with its coverage caveat (Jeff 2026-11-22: "Homicide Reports"); NIBRS answers only a detail only NIBRS holds. A current-year request goes to the current-year source, with its completeness caveats (and P52).
exact default or choices offered: Source by question type, as above; each answer names its source and coverage (D30).
why: The Crime Index is the website that collects current and historical data: national estimates for the seven UCR Part I offenses back to 1960, and state totals and rates for the seven from 1960 to 2025. Consistent with P01 and D32 (completed years from these figures, not NIBRS). The dataset is crimeindex.org's historical_crime table (public export /api/download?dataset=historical_crime), confirmed by Jeff 2026-10-29.
status: Decided 2026-10-29 (Jeff: "state and national totals should come from the Crime Index dataset, it should all already be calculated"; "UCR Part I offense -- one of those 7 it goes to the national figures we have on the crime index. It has national estimates for the 7 ucr part 1 crimes back to 1960 and state crime totals and rates for the 7 ucr part 1 offenses from 1960 to 2025"; on the historical_crime export: "yes, that's it, state and national totals for every year since 1960"); Jeff 2026-11-22 (audit B14: "Homicide Reports"): any murder detail goes to Homicide Reports
